note: Hand-written golden transcripts for the proxy's OpenAI Responses codec. `host` is the item list (request.input), not the whole request body: instructions are outside it and are carried by the daemon. The item list is FLAT, so each top-level item becomes one core Message holding the translated part, and the item's own `type` rides along so encode knows whether to emit a top-level item or a message. The `function-call-raw-arguments` case pins the sharpest trap: `arguments` is a JSON *string*, and a codec that re-serialises it changes bytes even though the data is identical.

cases.name: plain-turns
cases.note: The baseline: input_text on the user side, output_text on the assistant side.

content.text: Summarise the plugin in one line.
It bounds the context window with an explicit state.

cases.name: function-call-pair
cases.note: A function_call and its function_call_output as top-level items, which is why the codec cannot be identity here: both must reach the core as the same shape the Anthropic codec produces.

cases.name: encrypted-reasoning
cases.note: A reasoning item carrying encrypted_content the core must not read but must hand back untouched. The summary is a list of summary_text parts, so the codec must flatten it without losing the list on the way back.

summary.text: The user wants the pairing arithmetic checked.

cases.name: function-call-raw-arguments
cases.note: The whitespace trap: this `arguments` string has spaces after the colons, so JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(s)) is NOT s. The codec must leave the raw string on the part and only fall back to stringify for a part it created itself.

cases.name: unknown-fields
cases.note: Item fields the core vocabulary does not name - a web_search_call and a reasoning item with an content block - so a codec that constructs rather than spreads drops them.
